sourceDate.text: 與是儀、徐詳俱典軍國密事
權使綜與賀齊輕行掩襲

units.zh: 是儀字子羽，北海營陵人也。
units.en: Shi Yi (courtesy Ziyu) came from Yingling in Beihai commandery.
units.literal: Shi Yi, courtesy name Ziyu, was a man of Yingling in Beihai.

units.zh: 本姓氏，初為縣吏，後仕郡。
units.en: His clan name had been Shi; he began as a county clerk and later entered commandery service.
units.literal: Originally his surname was Shi; at first he was a county clerk, afterward he served the commandery.

units.zh: 郡相孔融嘲儀，言"氏"字"民"無上，可改為"是"，乃遂改焉。
units.en: Commandery chief Kong Rong teased him that the graph for his surname looked like the people radical with nothing sovereign above it, and jokingly suggested he adopt the homophone meaning "yes"—so he did.
units.literal: The commandery administrator Kong Rong mocked Yi, saying the character shi written as "clan" has "people" without a "ruler" above—it could be changed to shi meaning "yes"—thereupon he changed it.

units.zh: 〈徐众评曰：古之建姓，或以所生，或以官号，或以祖名，皆有义体，以明氏族。
units.en: 〈Commentator Xu Zhong remarks that ancient surnames were coined from birth tokens, offices, or forebears' names—each carried meaning that bound a lineage together.
units.literal: 〈Xu Zhong's appraisal states: In ancient times in establishing surnames, some by what was born, some by office titles, some by ancestors' names—all had meaningful forms to clarify clan families.

units.zh: 故曰胙之以土而命之氏，此先王之典也，所以明本重始，彰示功德，子孙不忘也。
units.en: Hence the ritual formula: grant land and bestow the clan name—former kings used that to mark origins, celebrate merit, and keep descendants mindful of their roots.
units.literal: Therefore it is said they enfeoffed them with soil and thereby commanded their clan name—this is the canon of former kings, whereby to clarify the root and honor beginnings, display merit and virtue, so descendants do not forget.

units.zh: 今离文析字，横生忌讳，使仪易姓，忘本诬祖，不亦谬哉！
units.en: To split characters for superstitious puns and make a man discard his surname is to sever him from his ancestors—surely that is folly.
units.literal: Now splitting graphs and analyzing characters, recklessly producing taboos, causing Yi to change surname, forgetting the root and slandering ancestors—is this not erroneous!

units.zh: 教人易姓，从人改族，融既失之，仪又不得也。〉
units.en: To urge another to change his lineage was Kong Rong's mistake; Shi Yi ought not to have complied.〉
units.literal: Teaching people to change surname, following others in altering clan—Kong Rong already missed the mark, and Yi too did not get it right.〉

units.zh: 後依劉繇，避亂江東。
units.en: He then joined Liu Yao and crossed south to escape the wars.
units.literal: Afterward he attached himself to Liu Yao, fleeing turmoil to the east of the Yangzi.

units.zh: 繇軍改，儀徙會稽。
units.en: After Liu Yao's defeat he resettled in Kuaiji.
units.literal: When Yao's army was defeated, Yi moved to Kuaiji.

units.zh: 孫權承攝大業，優文征儀。
units.en: Sun Quan, taking charge of Wu's destiny, sent him a warm letter of invitation.
units.literal: When Sun Quan assumed regency of the great enterprise, he issued a gracious summons recruiting Yi.

units.zh: 到見親任，專典機密，拜騎都尉。
units.en: Once he arrived he won Sun Quan's confidence, handled confidential affairs, and was named chief of the capitals grooms.
units.literal: When he arrived he was treated as intimate and trusted, exclusively managing secret matters, and was appointed Chief of the Capitals Grooms.

units.zh: 呂蒙圖襲關羽，權以問儀，儀善其計，勸權聽之。
units.en: When Lü Meng planned the strike on Guan Yu, Sun Quan consulted Shi Yi, who endorsed the scheme and urged him to act.
units.literal: Lü Meng plotted a surprise attack on Guan Yu; Quan asked Yi about it; Yi approved the plan and urged Quan to heed it.

units.zh: 從討羽，拜忠義校尉。
units.en: He accompanied the campaign against Guan Yu and received the rank of colonel of loyalty and righteousness.
units.literal: He followed in the punitive expedition against Yu and was appointed Colonel of Loyalty and Righteousness.

units.zh: 儀陳謝，權令曰："孤雖非趙簡子，卿安得不自屈為周捨邪？
units.en: Shi Yi tried to decline; Sun Quan told him, "I may not be Zhao Jianzi, but will you not humble yourself as Zhou She did for him?"
units.literal: Yi offered thanks in declination; Quan issued an order saying: "Although I am not Zhao Jianzi, how can you refuse to humble yourself and be my Zhou She?"

units.zh: "既定荊州，都武昌，拜裨將軍，後封都亭侯，守侍中。
units.en: After Jingzhou fell the court moved to Wuchang, where Shi Yi became a subordinate general (pi jiangjun), then village marquis of the capital precinct, while remaining palace attendant.
units.literal: "After Jingzhou was settled, the capital was established at Wuchang; he was appointed General of the Rear Guard, later enfeoffed as village marquis of the capital precinct, and kept as palace attendant.

units.zh: 欲復授兵，儀自以非材，固辭不受。
units.en: Sun Quan later offered him a military command; Shi Yi, judging himself no soldier, refused firmly.
units.literal: When Quan wished again to confer troops, Yi considered himself without martial talent and firmly declined and did not accept.

units.zh: 黃武中，遣儀之皖就將軍劉邵，欲誘致曹休。
units.en: During Huangwu he sent Shi Yi to Wan to work with General Liu Shao on the ruse to draw Cao Xiu forward.
units.literal: In the Huangwu period he dispatched Yi to Wan to join General Liu Shao, intending to lure Cao Xiu to come.

units.zh: 休到，大破之，遷偏將軍，入闕省尚書事，外總平諸官，兼領辭訟，又令都諸公於書學。
units.en: Cao Xiu walked into the trap and was crushed; Shi Yi rose to lieutenant general, took charge of Secretariat review, coordinated civil offices, heard lawsuits, and oversaw the palace school of writing.
units.literal: When Xiu arrived, he was greatly defeated; Yi was promoted to lieutenant general, entered the court to inspect Secretariat business, outwardly oversaw the leveling of all offices, concurrently managed litigation, and was also ordered to supervise the gentlemen in calligraphy study.

units.zh: 大駕東遷，太子登留鎮武昌，使儀輔太子。
units.en: When Sun Quan shifted east, Crown Prince Sun Deng stayed to hold Wuchang with Shi Yi as his aide.
units.literal: When the great chariot moved east, the heir Deng remained to guard Wuchang, and Quan ordered Yi to assist the heir.

units.zh: 太子敬之，事先咨詢，然後施行。
units.en: The crown prince honored him and never acted on policy until he had asked his advice.
units.literal: The heir respected him; in affairs he first consulted him, then carried them out.

units.zh: 進封都鄉侯。
units.en: His fief was raised to capital-district village marquis.
units.literal: He was advanced in fief to village marquis of the capital district.

units.zh: 後從太子還建業，復拜侍中、中執法，平諸官事、領辭訟如舊。
units.en: He later accompanied the heir to Jianye and resumed palace attendant and central law enforcer, with the same civil and judicial duties.
units.literal: Later he followed the heir back to Jianye, and was again appointed palace attendant and central law enforcer, leveling all office business and managing litigation as before.

units.zh: 典校郎呂壹誣白故江夏太守刁嘉謗仙國政，權怒，收嘉系獄，悉驗問。
units.en: Inspector Lü Yi denounced former Jiangxia prefect Diao Jia for criticizing the throne; Sun Quan jailed Diao and ordered a full inquiry.
units.literal: The proofreading gentleman Lü Yi falsely reported that the former Administrator of Jiangxia Diao Jia had slandered immortal state policy; Quan was angry, seized Jia and bound him in prison, and fully interrogated.

units.zh: 時同坐人皆怖畏壹，並言聞之，儀獨雲無聞。
units.en: Everyone present feared Lü Yi and claimed to have heard the slander—only Shi Yi said he had heard nothing.
units.literal: At the time those sitting together were all in fear of Yi, and together said they had heard it; Yi alone said he had not heard.

units.zh: 於是見窮詰累日，詔旨轉厲，群臣為之屏息。
units.en: For days the interrogators pressed him while the emperor's tone hardened; the whole court held its breath.
units.literal: Thereupon he was subjected to harsh questioning for successive days; the edict's intent turned severe, and the host of ministers held their breath for him.

units.zh: 儀對曰："今刀鋸已在臣頸，臣何敢為嘉隱諱，自取夷滅，為不忠之鬼!顧以聞知當有本末。
units.en: Shi Yi answered, "The executioner's blade is at my throat; I would not lie to shield Diao Jia and die a traitor's death—yet anything truly heard has a clear beginning and end."
units.literal: Yi replied: "Now the knife and saw are already on your subject's neck—how dare your subject for Jia conceal and cover, bringing extinction on himself and becoming a ghost of disloyalty! Only what I have heard ought to have beginning and end.

units.zh: "據實答問，辭不傾移。
units.en: He stuck to the facts and never shifted his story.
units.literal: "He answered questions according to fact, and his wording did not shift or tilt.

units.zh: 權遂捨之，嘉亦得免。
units.en: Sun Quan dropped the case, and Diao Jia went free.
units.literal: Quan thereupon released him, and Jia also obtained exemption.

units.zh: 〈徐众评曰：是仪以羁旅异方，客仕吴朝，值谗邪殄行，当严毅之威，命县漏刻，祸急危机，不雷同以害人，不苟免以伤义，可谓忠勇公正之士，虽祁奚之免叔向，庆忌之济硃云，何以尚之？
units.en: 〈Xu Zhong praises him as a stranger in Wu who, when slander threatened an innocent life, refused to parrot lies or save his skin at the cost of honor—loyal, brave, and just, rivaling the finest exemplars of old.
units.literal: 〈Xu Zhong's appraisal states: Shi Yi, a traveler in a strange region, guest-serving the Wu court, encountered slanderous evil running its course, faced stern and severe might, his life hung by the clepsydra's drip, disaster urgent in a moment of crisis—he did not echo others to harm people, nor seek careless escape to wound righteousness—he may be called a loyal, brave, and upright gentleman; even Qi Xi's freeing Shu Xiang or Qing Ji's aiding Zhu Yun—how could they surpass this?

units.zh: 忠不谄君，勇不慑耸，公不存私，正不党邪，资此四德，加之以文敏，崇之以谦约，履之以和顺，保傅二宫，存身爱名，不亦宜乎！〉
units.en: He was loyal without flattery, resolute without swagger, fair without favor, upright without faction—add wit, humility, and gentleness, and you have the ideal guardian for both heirs.〉
units.literal: Loyal and not flattering the lord, brave and not cowering, fair and not storing private bias, upright and not factioning with evil—endowed with these four virtues, augmented by literary quickness, exalted by modest restraint, practiced with mild compliance, guarding the two palaces as tutor and protector, preserving body and cherishing name—is this not fitting!〉

units.zh: 蜀相諸葛亮卒，權垂心西州，遣儀使蜀申固盟好。
units.en: After Zhuge Liang's death Sun Quan turned his eyes westward and sent Shi Yi to Chengdu to renew the alliance.
units.literal: When Shu's Chancellor Zhuge Liang died, Quan hung his heart on the western provinces and dispatched Yi as envoy to Shu to reaffirm the covenant of friendship.

units.zh: 奉使稱意，後拜尚書僕射。
units.en: The embassy succeeded, and he was promoted to secretariat supervisor.
units.literal: He fulfilled the mission to satisfaction, and afterward was appointed Supervisor of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 南、魯二宮初立，儀以本職領魯王傅。
units.en: When the Heir Apparent and Prince of Lu each received a household, Shi Yi kept his offices and became tutor to the Prince of Lu.
units.literal: When the southern and Lu princely mansions were first established, Yi in his original post concurrently served as tutor to the Prince of Lu.

units.zh: 儀嫌二宮相近切，乃上疏曰："臣竊以魯王天挺懿德，兼資文武，當今之宜，宜鎮四方，為國藩輔。
units.en: He disliked having the two residences cheek by jowl and wrote, "The Prince of Lu is gifted in civil and military affairs; in my humble view he should be posted on the frontier as a pillar of the realm."
units.literal: Yi disliked that the two mansions stood too close and pressed on each other; thereupon he submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject privately considers that the Prince of Lu, heaven-endowed with fine virtue, combining civil and martial gifts, in what is fitting for the present age, ought to be stationed in the four directions as a screen and support for the state.

units.zh: 宣揚德美，廣耀威靈，乃國家之良規，海內所瞻望。
units.en: Let him broadcast Wu's virtue and majesty abroad—that is sound policy and what the realm expects.
units.literal: To spread and raise virtuous beauty, broadly display awesome numen, is the state's good plan and what within the seas look up to.

units.zh: 但臣言辭鄙野，不能究盡其意。
units.en: I am coarse of speech and cannot say it half so well.
units.literal: Only your subject's words are rustic and wild, unable fully to exhaust the meaning.

units.zh: 愚以二宮宜有降殺，正上下之序，明教化之本。
units.en: I beg you to set clear precedence between the two households so that rank and ritual instruction are unambiguous.
units.literal: Your foolish subject considers the two mansions ought to have graded precedence, rectifying the order of high and low, clarifying the root of instruction and transformation.

units.zh: "書三四上。
units.en: He sent up the same memorial three or four times.
units.literal: "He submitted the document three or four times.

units.zh: 為傅盡忠，動輒規諫；
units.en: As tutor he spoke his mind whenever duty required;
units.literal: As tutor he exhausted loyalty; in every move he remonstrated;

units.zh: 事上勤，與人恭。
units.en: he was tireless toward superiors and courteous to everyone.
units.literal: serving superiors he was diligent, with others he was respectful.

units.zh: 不治產業，不受施惠，為屋舍財足自容。
units.en: He built no fortune, accepted no gifts, and kept a house just large enough for his needs.
units.literal: He did not manage estates or industry, did not accept largesse, and built dwellings and wealth only sufficient to shelter himself.

units.zh: 鄰家有起大宅者，權出望見，問起大室者誰。
units.en: When a neighbor put up a grand mansion Sun Quan noticed it from the palace and asked whose it was.
units.literal: A neighbor raised a great mansion; Quan went out, looked, and saw it, and asked who was the one raising the great chamber.

units.zh: 左右對曰："似是儀家也。
units.en: Attendants said, "It looks like Shi Yi's place."
units.literal: Those at his left and right replied: "It seems to be Yi's household."

units.zh: "權曰："儀儉，必非也。
units.en: Sun Quan answered, "Shi Yi is too frugal—that cannot be his."
units.literal: "Quan said: "Yi is frugal—it surely is not he."

units.zh: "問果他家。
units.en: A check proved it was someone else's.
units.literal: "On inquiry it indeed was another's family.

units.zh: 其見知信如此。
units.en: Such was the ruler's faith in his austerity.
units.literal: Thus he was known and trusted.

units.zh: 服不精細，食不重膳，拯贍貧困，家無儲畜。
units.en: He wore plain cloth, ate simple meals, helped the needy, and kept no hoard at home.
units.literal: His garments were not fine-woven; his food did not double dishes; he rescued and supplied the poor, and his home had no stored surplus.

units.zh: 權聞之，幸儀捨，求視蔬飯，親嘗之，對之歎息，即增俸賜，益田宅。
units.en: Sun Quan called at his home, tasted his spare fare, sighed, and raised his stipend and land grants.
units.literal: When Quan heard of it, he visited Yi's lodging, asked to see his vegetables and rice, personally tasted them, sighed in his presence, and on the spot increased his salary and gifts and added fields and dwellings.

units.zh: 儀累辭讓，以恩為戚。
units.en: Shi Yi tried to refuse the extras, embarrassed by such bounty.
units.literal: Yi repeatedly declined, taking favor as a burden.

units.zh: 時時有所進達，未嘗盲人之短。
units.en: He recommended talent when he saw it but never gossiped about others' faults.
units.literal: From time to time he had recommendations to advance, yet never spoke blind of people's shortcomings.

units.zh: 權常責儀以不言事，無是所非，儀對曰："聖主在上，臣下守職，懼於不稱，實不敢以愚管之畜，上干天聽。
units.en: Sun Quan once scolded him for holding his tongue; Shi Yi answered, "Under a sage king each man has his charge; I fear falling short of mine and would not waste your ear with trifles."
units.literal: Quan often reproached Yi for not speaking on affairs—there was nothing he condemned—Yi replied: "With a sage lord above, ministers below guarding their posts, I fear not matching my duty and truly dare not, with the petty stock of my foolish tube, ascend to offend Heaven's hearing."

units.zh: "事國數十年，未嘗有過。
units.en: He served Wu for decades without a stain on his record.
units.literal: "He served the state for several decades and never had a fault.

units.zh: 呂壹歷白將相大臣，或一人以罪聞者數四，獨無以白儀。
units.en: Lü Yi impeached everyone, some officers four times over, yet never found a handle on Shi Yi.
units.literal: Lü Yi serially denounced generals and ministers—sometimes one person was reported by crime four times—yet alone had nothing with which to denounce Yi.

units.zh: 權歎曰："使人盡如是儀，當安用科法為?"
units.en: Sun Quan sighed, "If all my men were like Shi Yi, I could throw away the law codes."
units.literal: Quan sighed and said: "If people were all like Yi, what need would there be to use laws and standards?"

units.zh: 及寢疾，遺令素棺，斂以時服，務從省約，年八十一卒。
units.en: At his deathbed he ordered a plain coffin, everyday clothes for burial, and the simplest rites; he died at eighty-one.
units.literal: When he fell gravely ill, he left instructions for a plain coffin, dressing in timely garments, striving to follow economy; he died at age eighty-one.

units.zh: 胡綜字偉則。
units.en: Hu Zong (courtesy Weize)
units.literal: Hu Zong, courtesy name Weize.

units.zh: 汝南固始人也。
units.en: He came from Gushi in Runan commandery.
units.literal: He was a man of Gushi in Runan.

units.zh: 少孤，母將避難江東。
units.en: He was orphaned young; his mother brought him south across the Yangzi to escape the wars.
units.literal: He lost his father early; his mother took him to flee turmoil east of the Yangzi.

units.zh: 孫策領會稽太守，綜年十四，為門下循行，留吳與孫權共讀書。
units.en: When Sun Ce was administrator of Kuaiji, Zong at fourteen became a gate attendant and stayed in Wu to read with Sun Quan.
units.literal: When Sun Ce held the post of Administrator of Kuaiji, Zong at age fourteen served as a gate attendant, remaining in Wu to study with Sun Quan.

units.zh: 策薨，權為討虜將軍，以綜為金曹從事，從討黃祖，拜鄂長。
units.en: After Sun Ce's death Sun Quan became general who pacifies barbarians, made Zong a gold-bureau clerk, joined the campaign against Huang Zu, and named him prefect of E.
units.literal: When Ce died, Quan became General Who Pacifies Barbarians and appointed Zong clerk of the gold bureau; he followed in the punitive expedition against Huang Zu and was named Prefect of E.

units.zh: 權為將軍，都京，召綜還，為書部。
units.en: When Sun Quan took the title of general and fixed the capital, he recalled Zong to head the documentation office.
units.literal: When Quan became general and established the capital, he recalled Zong and made him head of the documentation office.

units.zh: 與是儀、徐詳俱典軍國密事。
units.en: With Shi Yi and Xu Xiang he jointly handled confidential military and state business.
units.literal: Together with Shi Yi and Xu Xiang he jointly managed confidential state and military affairs.

units.zh: 劉備下白帝，權以見兵少，使綜料諸縣，得六千人，立解煩兩部，詳領左部、綜領右部督。
units.en: When Liu Bei came down from Baidi, Sun Quan, finding his visible troops too thin, had Zong levy the counties for six thousand men and formed two hardship-relief divisions—Xu Xiang led the left and Hu Zong the right.
units.literal: When Liu Bei descended from Baidi, Quan, seeing his visible forces were few, had Zong muster the counties and raise six thousand men, establishing two hardship-relief divisions—Xiang commanded the left division and Zong supervised the right.

units.zh: 吳將晉宗叛歸魏，魏以宗為蘄春太守，去江數百里，數為寇害。
units.en: The Wu officer Jin Zong crossed to Wei; Wei made him Qichun prefect hundreds of li from the river, and he raided the frontier again and again.
units.literal: The Wu officer Jin Zong defected to Wei; Wei appointed Zong Administrator of Qichun, several hundred li from the river, and he repeatedly raided as a bandit scourge.

units.zh: 權使綜與賀齊輕行掩襲，生虜得宗。
units.en: Sun Quan sent Zong with He Qi on a swift surprise raid and took Jin Zong alive.
units.literal: Quan sent Zong with He Qi on a light, swift ambush strike and captured Zong alive.

units.zh: 加建武中郎將。
units.en: He was promoted to central commander of establishing martial.
units.literal: He was promoted to Central Commander of Establishing Martial.

units.zh: 魏拜權為吳王，封綜、儀、詳皆為亭侯。
units.en: When Wei recognized Sun Quan as King of Wu, Zong, Yi, and Xiang were all made village marquises.
units.literal: When Wei invested Quan as King of Wu, Zong, Yi, and Xiang were all enfeoffed as village marquises.

units.zh: 黃武八年夏，黃龍見舉口，於是權稱尊號，因瑞改元。
units.en: That summer of 229 a yellow dragon was sighted at Jukou; Sun Quan thereupon took the imperial title and renamed the era after the omen.
units.literal: In the summer of the eighth year of Huangwu, a yellow dragon appeared at Jukou; thereupon Quan assumed the honored title and because of the omen changed the reign title.

units.zh: 又作黃龍大牙，常在中軍，諸軍進退，視其所向，命綜作賊曰：
units.en: He had a great yellow-dragon banner made for the central command; every column took its cue from it, and he commissioned Hu Zong to write a martial ode that begins:
units.literal: He also made a great yellow-dragon command pennant, constantly in the central army; the various armies' advance and withdrawal looked to where it pointed, and he ordered Zong to compose a piece on the bandit-enemy, saying:

units.zh: 乾坤肇立，三才是生。
units.en: Heaven and earth were fixed in place, and the three realms of nature took shape.
units.literal: Qian and Kun were first established, and the three powers came to be.

units.zh: 狼弧垂象，實惟兵精；
units.en: The Bow and Wolf constellations hung overhead—the very emblems of war;
units.literal: The Bow and Wolf stars hung their images—truly the essence of arms;

units.zh: 聖人觀法，是效是營，始作器械，爰求厥成。
units.en: the sage read their pattern, fashioned weapons after them, and brought the craft of war to perfection.
units.literal: the sage observed their pattern, modeled and planned them, first made weapons and tools, and thereby sought their completion.

units.zh: 黃、農創代，拓定皇基，上順天心，下息民災。
units.en: The Yellow Emperor and Shennong opened new eras, widened the royal foundation, matched heaven's will above, and stilled the people's woes below.
units.literal: The Yellow Thearch and Shennong founded ages, broadened and settled the imperial foundation, above complying with Heaven's heart, below resting the people's calamities.

units.zh: 高辛誅共，舜征有苗，啟有甘師，湯有鳴條。
units.en: Emperor Ku slew Gonggong; Shun chastised the Miao; Qi mustered the host of Gan; Tang struck at Mingtiao.
units.literal: Gaoxin executed Gong; Shun campaigned against the Miao; Qi had the host of Gan; Tang had Mingtiao.

units.zh: 周之牧野，漢之垓下，靡不由兵，克定厥緒。
units.en: Zhou won at Muye, Han at Gaixia—no mandate was settled without the sword.
units.literal: Zhou's Muye, Han's Gaixia—none were without arms; thereby they conquered and settled their threads.

units.zh: 明明大吳，實天生德，神武是經，惟皇之極。
units.en: Bright great Wu, heaven-taught in virtue, makes divine arms its warp and reaches the pole of kingship.
units.literal: Radiant great Wu—truly heaven-born in virtue; divine martiality is its warp, the utmost of majesty.

units.zh: 乃自在昔，黃、虞是祖，越歷五代，繼世在下。
units.en: From high antiquity, claiming the Yellow Emperor and Shun as forebears, your house endured five ages of exile before rising again.
units.literal: Thus from of old, taking the Yellow Thearch and Shun as ancestors, spanning five dynasties, generation after generation below.

units.zh: 應期受命，發跡南土，將恢大繇，革我區夏。
units.en: You answered the times, rose from the southern land, and set out to renew the great design and remake the heartland.
units.literal: Answering the period and receiving the mandate, you sprang from the southern soil, about to restore the great plan and transform our central states.

units.zh: 乃律天時，制為神軍，取象太一，五將三門；
units.en: You tuned the army to heaven's clock, formed a host on the Taiyi pattern—five commands, three gates;
units.literal: Then you harmonized with Heaven's seasons, fashioned a divine host, taking image from the Grand One—five generals, three gates;

units.zh: 疾則如電，遲則如雲，進止有度，約而不煩。
units.en: swift as lightning in the charge, broad as clouds in the pause—every movement measured, never chaotic.
units.literal: swift then like lightning, slow then like clouds; advance and halt have measure, restrained and not vexing.

units.zh: 四靈既布，黃龍處中，周制日月，實曰太常，桀然特立，六軍所望。
units.en: The four spirit guards take post, the yellow dragon holds the center like the Zhou king's Grand Constancy banner—lofty, alone, the cynosure of six hosts.
units.literal: The four numina deployed, the yellow dragon stands in the center; Zhou regulated sun and moon—truly called Grand Constancy; towering alone, the six armies look to it.

units.zh: 仙人在上，鑒觀四方，神實使之，為國休祥。
units.en: The immortal presence above watches every quarter; spirit drives the standard and brings good fortune to Wu.
units.literal: The transcendent above looks down on the four quarters; the spirit truly moves it, becoming auspicious blessing for the state.

units.zh: 軍欲轉向，黃龍先移，金鼓不鳴，寂然變施，暗謨若神，可謂秘奇。
units.en: When the line wheels, the dragon banner leads; drums need not roll—the host shifts in silent order, as if by hidden design.
units.literal: When the army wishes to turn, the yellow dragon moves first; metal drums need not sound—silently the deployment shifts; secret counsel like spirit—it may be called occult and marvelous.

units.zh: 在昔周室，赤烏銜書，今也大吳，黃龍吐符。
units.en: The Zhou saw a red crow bear its mandate; now great Wu sees the yellow dragon spit its sign.
units.literal: In olden Zhou's house the red crow carried the writ; now too great Wu— the yellow dragon spits the talisman.

units.zh: 合契河洛，動與道俱，天贊人和，歛曰惟休。
units.en: It matches the charts of the Yellow River and Luo, moves with the Dao—heaven approves, the people join—this is called supreme blessing.
units.literal: It matches the River and Luo, moves together with the Way; Heaven aids and men harmonize—gathered, it is called felicity.

units.zh: 蜀聞權踐阼，遣使重申前好。
units.en: Learning that Sun Quan had taken the throne, Shu sent envoys to renew the alliance.
units.literal: When Shu heard that Quan had ascended the throne, it dispatched envoys to reaffirm the former friendship.

units.zh: 綜為盟文，文義甚美，語在《權傳》。
units.en: Hu Zong drafted the treaty; the text was elegant—the full wording appears in Sun Quan's biography.
units.literal: Zong composed the covenant text; its literary meaning was very fine—the language is in the "Biography of Quan."

units.zh: 權下都建業，詳、綜並為侍中，進封鄉侯，兼左、右領軍。
units.en: After the court settled at Jianye, Xu Xiang and Hu Zong became joint palace attendants, village marquises, and left and right commanders of the guard.
units.literal: When Quan moved the capital down to Jianye, Xiang and Zong together became palace attendants, were advanced in fief to village marquises, and concurrently held left and right command of the guard.

units.zh: 時魏降人或雲魏都督河北振威將軍吳質頗見猜疑，綜乃偽質為作降文三條：
units.en: Wei turncoats claimed that Wu Zhi, Wei's Hebei commander and general who awes the foe, had fallen under suspicion; Hu Zong forged three "surrender" pieces in his name:
units.literal: At the time Wei defectors reported that Wei's area commander, General Who Inspires Awe north of the He, Wu Zhi, was much under suspicion; Zong thereupon forged for Zhi three articles of a surrender text:

units.zh: 其一曰：“天綱弛絕，四海分崩，群生憔悴，士人播越，兵寇所加，邑無居民，風塵煙火，往往而處。
units.en: The first begins: "The cosmic order has snapped; the realm is shattered; the people are worn thin and scholars wander homeless; where armies march, cities stand empty under a haze of war.
units.literal: The first says: "Heaven's net hangs slack, the four seas split and crumble; the throng of creatures is withered, gentlemen are scattered; where arms and bandits strike, towns lack dwellers; wind-blown dust and smoke of war are the usual sights.

units.zh: 自三代以來，大亂之極，未有若今時者也。
units.en: Since the Three Dynasties there has been no chaos to match this age.
units.literal: Since the Three Dynasties, at the extreme of great chaos, there has been none like the present time.

units.zh: 臣質志薄，處時無方，繫於土壤，不能翻飛，遂為曹氏執事戎役。
units.en: I, Wu Zhi, am a man of small ambition, pinned to the north with no way to fly free, and so I serve the Cao house in arms.
units.literal: Your subject Zhi's aims are slight; placed in the times without method, tied to the soil, unable to soar aloft, thereupon for the Cao clan he holds office in military service.

units.zh: 遠處河朔，天衢隔絕，雖望風慕義，思托大命，愧無因緣，得展其志。
units.en: The imperial road is blocked to me on the northern plain; though I long to join your righteous cause, I have had no opening—until now.
units.literal: Far removed on the northern He, the celestial thoroughfare is cut off; although I admire righteousness from afar and wish to entrust myself to the great mandate, I shamefully lack the connection to unfold my intent.

units.zh: 每往來者，竊聽風化，伏知陛下齊德乾坤，同明日月，神武之姿，受之自然。
units.en: From every traveler I glean news of your rule: you match heaven and earth in virtue, share light with the sun and moon, and your martial majesty is nature's own gift.
units.literal: Whenever travelers come and go, I secretly listen to their tidings of custom; prostrate I know that Your Majesty matches virtue with Qian and Kun, shares brightness with sun and moon, and the bearing of divine martiality is received from nature.

units.zh: 敷演皇極，流化萬里，自江以南，戶受覆燾。
units.en: You extend the royal polestar; your civilizing sway runs ten thousand li; south of the river every hearth rests beneath your wing.
units.literal: You spread the supreme pivot, your transforming influence flows ten thousand li; from south of the Yangzi every household receives your covering shade.

units.zh: 英雄俊傑，上達之士，莫不心歌腹詠，樂在歸附者也。
units.en: Every hero and man of note sings your praise in secret and yearns to come over.
units.literal: Heroes and outstanding men, gentlemen who rise to eminence—none do not sing in heart and chant in belly, rejoicing to attach themselves.

units.zh: 今年六月末，奉聞吉日，龍興踐阼，恢弘大繇，整理天綱，將使遺民，睹見定主。
units.en: At the close of the sixth month I learned of your accession: the dragon has mounted the throne, widened the great design, and restored order so that lost folk may at last see their true sovereign.
units.literal: This year at the end of the sixth month I heard the auspicious day: the dragon rose and ascended the throne, expanding the great plan, setting Heaven's net in order, about to let the surviving people behold a settled lord.

units.zh: 營武王伐殷，殷氏倒戈；
units.en: When King Wu marched on Shang, the Shang warriors lowered their blades;
units.literal: When King Wu of Zhou campaigned against Yin, the Yin clan turned their spears;

units.zh: 高祖誅項，四面楚歌。
units.en: Gaozu struck down Xiang Yu while Chu songs rose on every side.
units.literal: the High Ancestor executed Xiang Yu, and on four sides Chu songs arose.

units.zh: 方之今日，未足以喻。
units.en: Those old stories scarcely match the joy of your accession.
units.literal: Compared to today, they are not enough to serve as likeness.

units.zh: 臣質不勝吳天至願，謹遣所親同郡黃定恭行奉表，及托降叛，間關求達，其欲所陳，載列於左。”
units.en: I cannot contain my longing for your mandate; I send my kinsman Huang Ding with this memorial, threading the border by devious routes—my full plea is set out below."
units.literal: Your subject Zhi cannot overcome his utmost wish toward august Heaven; respectfully he dispatches his intimate, fellow townsman Huang Ding, reverently to present a memorial, and relying on the channel of surrender and rebellion, by perilous paths seeks to reach you—what he wishes to state is arrayed at left."

units.zh: 其二曰：“昔伊尹去夏人商，陳平委楚歸漢，書功竹帛，遺名陵後世，世主不謂之背誕者，以為知天命也。
units.en: The second reads: "Long ago Yi Yin left Xia for Shang and Chen Ping abandoned Chu for Han; their deeds were recorded on bamboo and silk and their names endure for posterity—rulers did not call them traitors, but men who read Heaven's mandate.
units.literal: The second says: "In olden days Yi Yin left Xia for Shang, and Chen Ping abandoned Chu for Han; their merits were written on bamboo and silk and their names left mounds for later ages—sovereigns did not call them traitorous, deeming them men who knew Heaven's mandate.

units.zh: 臣昔為曹氏所見交接，外托群臣，內如骨肉，恩義綢繆，有合無離，遂受偏方之任，總河北之軍。
units.en: I was once taken in by the Cao house—outwardly a minister, inwardly treated like kin; our bond was close and unbroken, and I received a frontier command over the Hebei armies.
units.literal: Your subject was once received and connected by the Cao clan—outwardly among ministers, inwardly like flesh and bone; grace and duty were close-woven, joined without parting—thereupon he received a regional command and oversaw the armies north of the He.

units.zh: 當此之時，志望高大，永與曹氏同死懼生。
units.en: In those days my ambition was high; I meant to live and die with the Cao house.
units.literal: At that time his aims were lofty; he would forever share death and fear life with the Cao clan.

units.zh: 惟恐功之不建，事之不成耳。
units.en: I feared only that our work would fail and our cause come to nothing.
units.literal: He only feared that merit would not be established and affairs would not succeed.

units.zh: 及曹氏之亡，後嗣繼位，幼沖統政，讒言彌興。
units.en: After Cao Cao's death the heir took the throne—a child in power—and slander multiplied.
units.literal: When the Cao clan's founder died, the successor ascended, a youth holding government; slanderous words spread ever more.

units.zh: 同儕者以勢相害，異趣者得間其言，而臣受性簡略，素不下人，視彼數子，意實迫之，此亦臣之過也。
units.en: Colleagues preyed on one another; rivals seized on their talk; and I, blunt by nature and never humble before others, had pressed those men hard—this too was my fault.
units.literal: Peers harmed one another by power; those of different bent found openings in their words; yet your subject by nature is plain and brief, never deferring to others—looking on those several men, he truly pressed them—this too is your subject's fault.

units.zh: 遂為邪議所見構會，招至猜疑，誣臣欲叛。
units.en: Evil counsel framed me, suspicion followed, and I was accused of plotting rebellion.
units.literal: Thereupon he was framed by evil talk and brought under suspicion, falsely accused of wishing to rebel.

units.zh: 雖識真者保明其心，世亂讒勝，余嫌猶在，常懼一旦橫受無辜，憂心孔疚，如覆冰炭。
units.en: Though those who knew me cleared my name, in these troubled times calumny wins and doubt lingers; I live in dread of sudden injustice, my heart torn as between ice and fire.
units.literal: Although those who knew the truth vouched for his heart, in a chaotic age slander prevailed and lingering suspicion remained; he constantly feared suddenly suffering innocence by violence—his heart deeply afflicted, as if overturned between ice and fire.

units.zh: 昔樂毅為燕昭王立功於齊，惠王即位，疑奪其任，遂去燕之趙，休烈不虧。
units.en: Once Yue Yi served King Zhao of Yan against Qi; when King Hui came to the throne he was suspected and stripped of command, left Yan for Zhao, and lost none of his renown.
units.literal: Formerly Yue Yi for King Zhao of Yan achieved merit in Qi; when King Hui ascended, suspecting him he removed his charge, whereupon he left Yan for Zhao—his splendid fame undiminished.

units.zh: 彼豈欲二三其德，蓋畏功名不建，而懼禍之將及也。
units.en: Was he fickle in loyalty? He feared his achievements would come to nothing and ruin was closing in.
units.literal: Did he wish to double his virtue? He feared merit and fame would not be established and disaster was about to reach him.

units.zh: 昔遣魏郡周光以賈販為名，托叛南詣，宣達密計。
units.en: I once sent Zhou Guang of Wei commandery south disguised as a peddler, pretending to defect, to convey a secret design.
units.literal: Formerly he dispatched Zhou Guang of Wei commandery under the name of a merchant-trader, feigning defection to go south and declare the secret plan.

units.zh: 時以倉卒，未敢便有章表，使光口傳而已。
units.en: In the rush I dared not send a formal memorial and had Guang speak the message orally.
units.literal: At the time, because of haste, he dared not at once submit a formal memorial and had Guang transmit it by word alone.

units.zh: 以為天下大歸可見，天意所在，非吳復誰?此方之民，思為臣妾，延頸舉踵，惟恐兵來之遲耳。
units.en: I believed the realm's great allegiance was plain and Heaven's choice obvious—if not Wu, then who? The folk here long to submit, craning their necks and rising on tiptoe, dreading only that your armies arrive too late.
units.literal: He considered that the great return of All under Heaven was visible and Heaven's intent lay elsewhere—if not Wu, then who? The people of this region wish to become subjects; they stretch necks and lift heels, fearing only that troops come too late.

units.zh: 若使聖恩少加信納，當以河北承望王師，疑心赤實，天日是鑒。
units.en: If Your Majesty would grant a little trust, I would hold Hebei open for your host—my loyal heart is true; Heaven and sun bear witness.
units.literal: If Your sacred grace would slightly add trust and acceptance, he would from Hebei await the royal host—his loyal heart true red; sun and Heaven are witness.

units.zh: 而光去經年，不聞咳唾，未審此意竟得達不?瞻望長歎，日月以幾，魯望高子，何足以喻!又臣今日見待稍薄，蒼蠅之聲，綿綿不絕，必受此禍，遲速事耳。
units.en: Yet Guang left a year ago and not a word has returned—did my message ever reach you? I gaze south and sigh as the months pass; even Lu’s longing for Gaozi scarcely matches this! And now I am treated coldly; slander never stops—I am sure to suffer for it, only sooner or later.
units.literal: Yet Guang departed a year ago and no cough or spit has been heard—does this intent in the end reach you? Gazing afar he sighs long; days and months pile up—Lu Wang and Gao Zi are not enough as likeness! Moreover your subject today is treated somewhat thinly; the buzz of flies is unending—he is sure to suffer this calamity; it is only a matter of sooner or later.

units.zh: 臣私度陛下未垂明慰者，必以臣質貫穿仁義之道，不行若此之事，謂光所傳，多虛少實，或謂比中有他消息，不知臣質構讒見疑，恐受大害也。
units.en: I suppose Your Majesty has not yet reassured me because you take me for a man steeped in righteousness who would never act thus—thinking Guang's tale mostly false, or that some other intrigue is afoot—unaware that I am slandered and in peril.
units.literal: Your subject privately surmises that if Your Majesty has not yet extended clear comfort, it must be because your subject Zhi is thought to pierce through the Way of benevolence and righteousness and would not do such a thing—deeming what Guang transmitted mostly empty and little real, or that among these matters there is other news—not knowing your subject Zhi is framed by slander and suspected, fearing great harm.

units.zh: 且臣質著有罪之日，自當奔赴鼎鑊，束身待罪，此蓋人臣之宜也。
units.en: And if I were truly guilty I would go bound to the executioner's cauldron—that is a subject's duty.
units.literal: Moreover, on a day when your subject Zhi is clearly guilty, he ought of himself to rush to the tripod and the cauldron, binding his body to await punishment—this is what a minister should do.

units.zh: 今日無罪，橫見譖毀，將有商鞅、白起之禍。
units.en: Today, innocent, I am suddenly defamed and face the fate of Shang Yang or Bai Qi.
units.literal: Today without guilt he is suddenly slandered and will meet the calamity of Shang Yang and Bai Qi.

units.zh: 尋惟事勢，去亦直也。
units.en: Weighing the situation, departure is the honest course.
units.literal: Reflecting on the situation, to leave is also straight.

units.zh: 死而弗義，不去何為!樂毅之出，吳起之走，君子傷其不遇，未有非之者也。
units.en: To die without justice—why not leave? When Yue Yi left and Wu Qi fled, gentlemen mourned their ill treatment; none blamed them.
units.literal: To die without righteousness—if he does not leave, what is he to do! Yue Yi's departure, Wu Qi's flight—gentlemen grieve their lack of recognition; none have condemned them.

units.zh: 願陛下推古況今，不疑怪於臣質也。
units.en: I beg Your Majesty to weigh antiquity against today and not find me strange.
units.literal: May Your Majesty extend ancient examples to judge the present and not be suspicious or strange toward your subject Zhi.

units.zh: 又念人臣獲罪，當如伍員奉己自效，不當繞幸因事為利。
units.en: I know a guilty minister should, like Wu Zixu, offer himself in loyal service—not twist events for private gain.
units.literal: He also reflects that when a minister receives guilt, he ought like Wu Yuan to offer himself in service, not seek advantage by circling fortune and using events for profit.

units.zh: 然今與古，厥勢不同，南北悠遠。
units.en: Yet today differs from antiquity; north and south are far apart.
units.literal: Yet now and antiquity—their situations differ; north and south are vast and far.

units.zh: 江湖隔絕，自不舉事，何得濟免!是以忘志士之節，而思立功之義也之也。
units.en: Rivers and lakes stand between us—without acting myself, how could I escape? So I set aside pure integrity and think instead of earning merit by service.
units.literal: Rivers and lakes cut off—if he himself does not act, how can he cross to safety! Therefore forgetting the integrity of a resolute man, he thinks instead of the righteousness of establishing merit.

units.zh: 且臣質又以曹氏之嗣，非天命所在，政弱刑亂，柄奪於臣，諸將專威於外，各自為政，莫或同心，士卒衰耗，帑藏空虛，綱紀毀廢，上下並昏，想前後數得降叛，具聞此問，兼弱攻昧，宜應天時，此實陛下進取之秋。
units.en: I also judge the Cao heir not Heaven's choice—weak rule, chaotic law, power held by ministers; generals rule their own domains abroad without unity; troops waste away and coffers stand empty; order is broken and court and country are blind. Your Majesty has heard this from many deserters: strike the weak while fortune favors you—this is your moment to advance.
units.literal: Moreover your subject Zhi also considers that the Cao successor is not where Heaven's mandate lies—government weak, punishments chaotic, the handle seized by ministers; generals wield sole might abroad, each governing on his own, none of one heart; soldiers decline and waste; treasury stores are empty; statutes and discipline are ruined and abandoned; high and low alike are benighted. He thinks that from front and back you have repeatedly received defectors and rebels and fully heard this inquiry—attack the weak and strike the dim, fit Heaven's season—this is truly the season for Your Majesty's advance.

units.zh: 是以區區敢獻其計。
units.en: In my small way I dare offer this plan.
units.literal: Therefore in his slight way he dares offer this plan.

units.zh: 今若內兵淮、泗，據有下邳，荊、揚二州，聞聲響應，臣從河北席眷而南，形勢一連，根牙永固。
units.en: If you march on the Huai and Si and seize Xiapi, Jing and Yang will answer at once; I will roll south from Hebei, our positions will link, and the foundation will hold.
units.literal: Now if inner troops move on the Huai and Si, hold Xiapi, and the two provinces Jing and Yang respond at the sound, your subject from Hebei rolls up his mat-rug and goes south—the situation links as one, root and branch forever firm.

units.zh: 關西之兵繫於所衛，青、徐二州不敢徹守，許，洛余兵眾不滿萬，誰能來東與陛下爭者?此城千載一會之期，可不深思而熟計乎!及臣所在，既自多馬，加以羌、胡常以三四月中美草時，驅馬來出，隱度今者，可得三千餘匹。
units.en: Guansi's armies are pinned to their posts; Qing and Xu dare not strip their garrisons; fewer than ten thousand men remain at Xu and Luoyang—who could march east against you? This is a once-in-a-millennium chance—will you not weigh it carefully? Where I am we already have many horses; in the third and fourth months, when grass is rich, the Qiang and Hu drive herds out—I estimate three thousand mounts could be gathered now.
units.literal: The troops of Guanxi are tied to what they guard; the two provinces Qing and Xu dare not fully withdraw garrisons; at Xu and Luo the remaining soldiers number less than ten thousand—who can come east to contend with Your Majesty? This is a once-in-a-thousand-years meeting—can you not deeply ponder and carefully plan! As to where your subject is, he already has many horses; moreover the Qiang and Hu often in the third and fourth months, when grass is lush, drive horses out—privately estimating the present, he could obtain more than three thousand head.

units.zh: 陛下出軍，當投此時，多將騎士來就馬耳。
units.en: Your Majesty should march at that season and send many horsemen to collect the mounts.
units.literal: When Your Majesty sends out the army, you should strike at this time, bringing many knights to come take the horses.

units.zh: 此皆先定所一二知。
units.en: These points I know well in advance.
units.literal: These are matters he knows beforehand one or two in advance.

units.zh: 凡兩軍不能相究虛實，今此間實羸，易可克定，陛下舉動，應者必多。
units.en: Armies cannot always probe each other's strength; this region is truly weak and easily taken—when you move, many will join you.
units.literal: In general two armies cannot investigate each other's emptiness and fullness; now this region is truly weak and easily conquered and settled—when Your Majesty acts, responders will surely be many.

units.zh: 上定洪業，使普天一統，下令臣質建非常之功，此乃天也。
units.en: To settle the great enterprise and unify the realm, and to let me win extraordinary merit—that is Heaven's will.
units.literal: Above, settling the great enterprise and making all under Heaven one—ordering your subject Zhi to establish extraordinary merit—this is Heaven.

units.zh: 若不見納，此亦天也。
units.en: If you refuse, that too is Heaven's decree.
units.literal: If not accepted, this too is Heaven.

units.zh: 願陛下思之，不復多陳。”
units.en: I beg Your Majesty to consider it; I will say no more."
units.literal: May Your Majesty ponder it; he will not further elaborate much."

units.zh: 其三曰：“昔遠子捨袁就曹，規畫計較，應見納受，遂破袁軍，以定曹業。
units.en: The third reads: "When Xu You left Yuan Shao for Cao Cao, his counsel was heeded, Yuan's host was broken, and Cao's power was secured.
units.literal: The third says: "Formerly Ziyuan left Yuan for Cao, planning and calculating; he was accepted and employed, thereupon he broke Yuan's army and settled Cao's enterprise.

units.zh: 向使曹氏不信子遠，懷疑猶豫，不決於心，則今天下袁氏有也。
units.en: Had Cao Cao doubted Xu You and hesitated, the realm would belong to the Yuans today.
units.literal: Had the Cao clan not trusted Ziyuan, harbored doubt and hesitation, not decided in the heart, then today All under Heaven would belong to the Yuan clan.

units.zh: 願陛下思之。
units.en: Think on that, Your Majesty.
units.literal: May Your Majesty ponder it.

units.zh: 間聞界上將閻浮、趙楫欲歸大化，唱和不速，以取破亡。
units.en: I hear frontier officers Yan Fu and Zhao Ji meant to come over but moved too slowly and were destroyed.
units.literal: Privately I have heard that the border generals Yan Fu and Zhao Ji wish to join your great transformation, but their concert was not swift, whereby they met defeat and ruin.

units.zh: 今臣款款，遠授其命，若復懷疑，不時舉動，令臣孤絕，受此厚禍，即恐天下雄夫烈士欲立功者，不敢復托命陛下矣，願陛下思之。
units.en: I offer my allegiance in good faith; if you delay and leave me exposed, every bold man who might serve you will think twice about crossing over—ponder that, I beg you.
units.literal: Now your subject, in utmost sincerity, from afar entrusts his mandate; if again you harbor doubt and do not act in good time, leaving your subject isolated to suffer this heavy calamity—then I fear that stalwart heroes under Heaven who wish to establish merit will not again dare entrust their lives to Your Majesty. May Your Majesty ponder it.

units.zh: 皇天后土，實聞其言。”
units.en: Heaven and earth are witness to this pledge."
units.literal: August Heaven and later soil truly hear these words."

units.zh: 此文既流行，而質已人為侍中矣。
units.en: By the time the forgery spread, the real Wu Zhi had already been appointed palace attendant in Wei.
units.literal: After this text had circulated, Zhi had already entered and become palace attendant.

units.zh: 二年，青州人隱蕃歸吳。
units.en: In the second year of that era a Qingzhou adventurer named Yin Fan crossed over to Wu.
units.literal: In the second year, a man of Qingzhou, Yin Fan, came over to Wu.

units.zh: 上書曰：“臣聞紂為無道，微子先出。
units.en: He presented a memorial: "I have heard that when Zhou was cruel, Weizi left the court first.
units.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject has heard that Zhou was without the Way, and Weizi departed first.

units.zh: 高祖寬明，陳平先入。
units.en: When Gaozu showed clemency, Chen Ping was first through the gate.
units.literal: The High Ancestor was magnanimous and clear-sighted, and Chen Ping entered first.

units.zh: 臣年二十二，委棄封域，歸命有道，賴蒙天靈，得自全致。
units.en: At twenty-two I abandoned my fief and came to a righteous sovereign; heaven spared me and I arrived intact.
units.literal: Your subject, at age twenty-two, cast aside his enfeoffed domain, returned his mandate to the possessor of the Way, and relying on receiving Heaven's numinous favor, was able to preserve himself whole.

units.zh: 臣至北有日，而主者同之降人，未見精別，使臣徽言妙旨，不得上達。
units.en: I have been here for days, yet your clerks lump me with common deserters and will not carry my plea upward.
units.literal: Your subject has been in the north some days, yet those in charge treat him like other defectors and have not discerned fine distinctions, so that your subject's subtle words and excellent points cannot ascend to be heard.

units.zh: 於邑三歎，曷惟其已。
units.en: I choke back sob after sob—there is no end to this grief.
units.literal: I sigh thrice in anguish—how can it be stopped!

units.zh: 謹詣闕拜章，乞蒙引見。”
units.en: I therefore present myself at the gate with this memorial and beg for an audience."
units.literal: Respectfully I have come to the palace gate to bow with a memorial, begging to receive a summons to audience."

units.zh: 權即召入。
units.en: Sun Quan had him brought in at once.
units.literal: Quan immediately summoned him to enter.

units.zh: 蕃謝答問，及陳時務，甚有辭觀。
units.en: Yin Fan parried the emperor's questions and discoursed on policy with striking eloquence.
units.literal: Fan gave thanks, answered questions, and set forth the affairs of the time—very fine in rhetorical display.

units.zh: 綜時侍坐，權問何如。
units.en: Hu Zong was present; Sun Quan asked his opinion of the man.
units.literal: Zong at the time was in attendance at the sitting; Quan asked how he was.

units.zh: 綜對曰："蕃上書，大語有似東方朔，巧捷詭辯有似彌衡。
units.en: Hu Zong said, His memorial sounds like Dongfang Shuo at his broadest and like Mi Heng at his sharpest.
units.literal: Zong replied: Fan's memorial—its grand language resembles Dongfang Shuo; its clever quickness and crafty disputation resembles Mi Heng.

units.zh: 而才皆不及。
units.en: But he is not their equal in genius.
units.literal: Yet in talent he reaches neither."

units.zh: "權又問可堪何官？
units.en: The emperor asked what post might suit him.
units.literal: Quan again asked what office he could bear.

units.zh: 綜對曰："未可以治民，且試以都輦小職。
units.en: Hu Zong answered, "Not yet a magistrate—give him a small post around the capital first."
units.literal: Zong replied: "Not yet fit to govern the people—for now try him in a minor capital conveyance duty."

units.zh: "權以蕃盛論刑獄，用為廷尉監。
units.en: Because Yin Fan spoke well of criminal law, Sun Quan made him an assistant in the ministry of justice.
units.literal: Quan, because Fan discoursed at length on penal cases, employed him as overseer of the commandant of justice.

units.zh: 左將軍朱據、廷尉郝普稱蕃有王佐之才，普尤與之親善，常怨歎其屈。
units.en: Zhu Ju, general of the left, and Hao Pu, chief justice, hailed him as ministerial timber; Hao Pu grew especially close and complained that such a man was underemployed.
units.literal: General of the Left Zhu Ju and Commandant of Justice Hao Pu praised Fan as having the talent of a king's assistant; Pu especially was intimate and friendly with him, often resenting and sighing that he was wronged.

units.zh: 後蕃謀叛，事覺伏誅，
units.en: Later Yin Fan plotted treason; when it leaked he was put to death.
units.literal: Later Fan plotted rebellion; when the affair was discovered he was executed.

units.zh: 〈吴录曰：蕃有口才，魏明帝使诈叛如吴，令求作廷尉职，重案大臣以离间之。
units.en: 〈The Wu Records say Cao Rui sent him south as a spy to angle for the post of commandant of justice and use reopened cases against high ministers to sow discord.
units.literal: 〈The Wu lu states: Fan had rhetorical skill; Emperor Ming of Wei sent him feigning defection to Wu, ordering him to seek the office of commandant of justice and reopen weighty cases against great ministers to sow discord.

units.zh: 既为廷尉监，众人以据、普与蕃亲善，常车马云集，宾客盈堂。
units.en: Once he held that office, Zhu Ju and Hao Pu were seen at his door so often that rumor painted a conspiracy.
units.literal: Once he became overseer of justice, the crowd, because Ju and Pu were intimate with Fan, constantly saw carriages and horses gather like clouds and guests fill the hall.

units.zh: 及至事觉，蕃亡走，捕得，考问党与，蕃无所言。
units.en: When the plot broke, Yin Fan ran, was caught, and under torture about accomplices said nothing.
units.literal: When the affair was discovered, Fan fled; he was captured and examined on accomplices—Fan said nothing.

units.zh: 吴主使将入，谓曰：“何乃以肌肉为人受毒乎？”
units.en: Sun Quan sent an officer to ask why he would let his body absorb another man's torture.
units.literal: The ruler of Wu sent a general in and said to him: "Why would you let your flesh take poison for another?"

units.zh: 蕃曰：“孙君，丈夫图事，岂有无伴！
units.en: Yin Fan replied, "My lord, a man who plays for high stakes always has partners.
units.literal: Fan said: "Lord Sun, when a man plots great things, how can he lack companions!

units.zh: 烈士死，不足相牵耳。”
units.en: A man of honor may die; he will not drag others down with him."
units.literal: When a resolute knight dies, it is not enough to drag others along."

units.zh: 遂闭口而死。
units.en: He shut his mouth and died.
units.literal: Thereupon he closed his mouth and died.

units.zh: 吴历曰：权问普：“卿前盛称蕃，又为之怨望朝廷，使蕃反叛，皆卿之由。”〉
units.en: The Wu Calendar records Sun Quan confronting Hao Pu: "You heaped praise on Yin Fan and grumbled against the court until he rebelled—that fault is yours."
units.literal: The Wu li states: Quan asked Pu: "You earlier lavishly praised Fan, and also on his behalf resented the court—making Fan rebel—all stems from you."

units.zh: 普見責自殺。
units.en: Hao Pu killed himself under the reproach.
units.literal: When Pu saw he was blamed, he committed suicide.

units.zh: 據禁止，歷時乃解。
units.en: Zhu Ju was confined for a long stretch before he was cleared.
units.literal: Ju was placed under confinement; only after a long time was it lifted.

units.zh: 拜綜偏將軍，兼左執法，領辭訟。
units.en: Hu Zong was promoted to lieutenant general, left law enforcer, and again put in charge of lawsuits.
units.literal: Zong was appointed lieutenant general, concurrently left law enforcer, in charge of litigation.

units.zh: 遼東之事，輔吳將軍張昭以諫權言辭切至，權亦大怒，其和協彼此，使之無隙，綜有力焉。
units.en: When the Liaodong campaign drove Zhang Zhao, general who assists Wu, to remonstrate in blistering terms and Sun Quan raged, Hu Zong helped heal the rift between sovereign and chief counselor.
units.literal: In the Liaodong affair, General Who Assists Wu Zhang Zhao in remonstrating with Quan used speech cutting and extreme; Quan also was greatly angry; that he reconciled and harmonized the two sides, causing them to have no rift—Zong had power therein.

units.zh: 性嗜酒，酒後歡呼極意，或推引杯觴，搏擊左右。
units.en: He loved wine; drunk, he would whoop with delight, shove the cups about, and even cuff his neighbors.
units.literal: By nature he loved wine; after wine he shouted for joy to the utmost, sometimes pushing and pulling cups and goblets, striking those to his left and right.

units.zh: 權愛其才，弗之責也。
units.en: Sun Quan prized his gifts and overlooked the excess.
units.literal: Quan loved his talent and did not blame him for it.

units.zh: 凡自權統事，諸文誥策命，鄰國書符，略皆綜之所造也。
units.en: From Sun Quan's accession onward, most edicts, patents, and diplomatic notes to rival courts came from Hu Zong's brush.
units.literal: From the time Quan took charge of affairs, all documents, edicts, patent orders, and letters and tally-documents to neighboring states—in outline all were composed by Zong.

units.zh: 初以內外多事，特立科，長吏遭喪，皆不得去，而數有犯者。
units.en: Early in his reign Sun Quan barred senior officials from quitting post for funerals, yet men kept breaking the rule.
units.literal: At first, because inner and outer had many affairs, they specially established a statute: chief officials encountering mourning all could not leave, yet repeatedly there were violators.

units.zh: 權患之，使朝臣下議。
units.en: Annoyed, he asked the court for a remedy.
units.literal: Quan worried over it and ordered court ministers to deliberate.

units.zh: 綜議以為宜定科文，示以大辟，行之一人，其後必絕。
units.en: Hu Zong urged a written statute and a single public execution to stop the practice cold.
units.literal: Zong deliberated that they ought to fix statute text, display capital punishment, carry it out on one man, and afterward it would surely cease.

units.zh: 遂用綜言，由是奔喪乃斷，
units.en: Sun Quan took his advice, and unauthorized leave for mourning ended.
units.literal: Thereupon they employed Zong's words; whereby rushing to funerals was cut off.

units.zh: 赤烏六年卒，子沖嗣。
units.en: He died in 243; his son Hu Chong inherited the fief.
units.literal: He died in the sixth year of Chiwu; his son Chong succeeded.

units.zh: 沖平和有文干，天紀中為中書令。
units.en: Hu Chong was even-tempered and literate; under the Tianji era he rose to director of the palace secretariat.
units.literal: Chong was mild and harmonious and had literary capability; in the Tianji period he became palace secretary director.

units.zh: 〈吴录曰：冲后仕晋尚书郎、吴郡太守。〉
units.en: 〈The Wu Records add that Hu Chong later served Jin as a secretariat gentleman and prefect of Wu commandery.〉
units.literal: 〈The Wu lu states: Later Chong served Jin as gentleman of the Secretariat and Administrator of Wu commandery.〉

units.zh: 徐詳者字子明，吳郡烏程人也，先綜死。
units.en: Xu Xiang, courtesy Ziming, came from Wucheng in Wu commandery and died before Hu Zong.
units.literal: Xu Xiang, courtesy name Ziming, was a man of Wucheng in Wu commandery; he died before Zong.

units.zh: 作者評論
units.en: Editorial comment.
units.literal: Author's commentary.

units.zh: 評曰：是儀、徐詳、胡綜，皆孫權之時干興事業者也。
units.en: The appraisal states that Shi Yi, Xu Xiang, and Hu Zong were the men who kept Sun Quan's government running.
units.literal: The appraisal states: Shi Yi, Xu Xiang, and Hu Zong—all were men who managed and raised the enterprise in Sun Quan's time.

units.zh: 儀清恪貞素，詳數通使命，綜文采才用，各見信任，譬之廣夏，其榱椽之佐乎!
units.en: Shi Yi was incorruptible, Xu Xiang a veteran envoy, Hu Zong a brilliant pen—all earned deep trust; they were the beams that held up Sun Quan's hall.
units.literal: Yi was pure, scrupulous, chaste, and plain; Xiang repeatedly carried out missions; Zong had literary brilliance and practical ability—each was seen and trusted; compare them to a broad hall—they were the ridgepole-and-rafter assistants!
